Quick update from ops side — initial checks:

- Grafana p95/p99 panels show a clear inflection at 07:54 UTC (attached grafana_p95_chart_0823.png). The spike aligns with a routing config change we pushed 2026-08-22T23:50:12Z (change id: cfg-rt-1137) intended to prefer regional egress optimization.
- Platform tracing shows an uptick in TCP RTT for requests labeled EU -> us-east-1 egress node (extra ~110-140ms).
- Error-rate increase corresponds to a small % of requests that hit a fallback model variant in us-east which has slightly different timeout behavior.

Hypothesis: a misapplied egress mapping rule caused a subset of EU traffic to be routed to us-east rather than eu-west. That would explain the added RTT and the p95/p99 regression.

I'm opening SUP-9821 and attaching the grafana snapshot. Laura, can you confirm if a rollback of cfg-rt-1137 is safe as a hotfix? If not, can we add a targeted routing override for VestorHealth until we complete a proper rollback?

Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sharp p95/p99 jump for EU-hosted traffic — urgent

Triage complete — short summary and mitigation plan below.

Root cause (confirmed): an egress mapping rule (cfg-rt-1137) deployed 2026-08-22 23:50:12Z accidentally included a broader prefix match. That caused ~12% of customer sessions from eu-west-1 to be routed to our us-east-1 egress pool. The extra cross-region RTT + occasional model fallback accounts for the p95/p99 jump and small error burst.

What we did so far:
- Opened Jira: SUP-9821 (tracking)
- Created a targeted override to pin VestorHealth traffic back to eu-west-1 (applied 2026-08-23T09:45:00Z) — preliminary metrics show p95 dropping back toward baseline for that flow.
- Prepared rollback patch for cfg-rt-1137 (egress_mapping_patch.diff) — ready for deploy with 30-minute canary.

Proposed next steps (action owners):
1) Deploy the rollback patch (Laura/Infra) with a 30-minute canary to eu-west-1 — ETA 30m.
2) Keep the targeted override for VestorHealth until 24h of stable metrics. (Marissa to monitor)
3) Postmortem & runbook update to prevent overly-broad prefix matches (Marissa/Laura)
4) Customer comms: send a short RCA + apology + goodwill credit offer (Karthik to own)

Hannah — flagging for exec visibility given customer escalation and potential SLA credit ask.

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Alice —

Thank you for the report and for the trace file you provided. Short summary of what happened and next steps:

What we found
- Root cause: a recent routing config (cfg-rt-1137) included an overly broad prefix and caused ~12% of EU sessions to be routed to our US egress pool, adding ~110–140ms to p95 and causing a small set of requests to hit a fallback model variant (increasing error rate).

What we did
- Applied a temporary targeted override to ensure your traffic stays in eu-west-1 (completed at 09:45 UTC).
- Preparing to roll back the problematic config with a careful 30-minute canary.
- Opened internal ticket SUP-9821 and will update you with final RCA and postmortem within 48 hours.

Next steps for you
- We recommend continuing to monitor the pilot group for the next hour and let us know if you see any residual anomalies.

Compensation
- I'm coordinating with our partner ops and finance teams to propose a goodwill credit for the affected window; I'll include that in the formal RCA.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand this impacts your pilot and execs. I'll update you immediately when the rollback completes and after the postmortem.
